title: Grade 8 Science — Thu, Jun 12
description: Metals and Non-metals — Day 4 of 5: Alloys, corrosion, and rust prevention
subject: science

questions.question: An alloy is a:
options: Mixture of two or more metals (or a metal and non-metal)
questions.explanation: An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of metals (or a metal with non-metals) to get improved properties.

questions.question: Steel is an alloy of iron and:
questions.explanation: Steel is an alloy of iron and carbon (0.2–2.1% carbon). Carbon makes iron stronger and harder.

questions.question: Stainless steel contains iron, carbon, and also ____ which prevents rusting.
questions.explanation: Stainless steel contains iron, carbon, and about 10–12% chromium (and sometimes nickel). Chromium forms a protective oxide layer.

questions.question: Brass is an alloy of:
questions.explanation: Brass = copper + zinc. It is harder than copper and used for musical instruments, taps, and decorative items.

questions.question: Bronze is an alloy of:
questions.explanation: Bronze = copper + tin. It was the first widely used metal alloy (Bronze Age). Used for sculptures, medals, and bearings.

questions.question: Corrosion is the process by which metals are:
options: Strengthened by chemical reactions with the environment
Slowly eaten away by chemical reactions with oxygen, moisture, or acids
questions.explanation: Corrosion is the deterioration of metals due to chemical reactions with oxygen, water, and other substances in the environment.

questions.question: Rusting of iron is an example of corrosion. The chemical name of rust is:
questions.explanation: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, Fe₂O₃·xH₂O. It forms when iron reacts with oxygen in the presence of moisture.

questions.question: Which two things are BOTH needed for iron to rust?
questions.explanation: Iron rusts only when both oxygen and water are present. Keeping iron dry or free from oxygen prevents rust.

questions.question: Galvanisation is the process of coating iron with ____ to prevent rusting.
questions.explanation: Galvanisation coats iron/steel with a layer of zinc. Zinc is more reactive, so it corrodes first (sacrificial protection).

questions.question: Painting iron bridges and gates prevents rust because:
options: Paint provides a barrier that prevents oxygen and water from reaching the iron
Paint contains acid that neutralises rust
questions.explanation: Paint acts as a physical barrier, preventing oxygen and moisture from contacting the iron surface and causing rust.

questions.question: Which alloy is used in aircraft and spacecraft because it is both light and strong?
questions.explanation: Duralumin is an aluminium alloy (Al + Cu + Mg) — very strong yet lightweight, ideal for aircraft construction.

questions.question: Tins used for food cans are steel coated with ____ to prevent reaction with food.
questions.explanation: Food cans are made of steel coated with a thin layer of tin (tinplate). Tin is less reactive and does not affect food.

questions.question: Which of these methods is NOT a rust prevention technique?
questions.explanation: Salt water accelerates rusting because it increases the conductivity of moisture around iron. It is the opposite of prevention.

questions.question: Solder, used to join electrical wires, is an alloy of:
questions.explanation: Traditional solder is an alloy of lead and tin with a low melting point, used to join metal components in electronics.

questions.question: Aluminium cans (used for cold drinks) do not rust. Why?
options: Aluminium forms a thin oxide layer that protects it from further corrosion
Aluminium is coated in zinc like iron
questions.explanation: Aluminium quickly forms Al₂O₃ (aluminium oxide) on its surface — a tough, invisible layer that prevents further corrosion.
